Colorado.sentenceCompletion: Includes jail time, probation, parole, and paying all fines and restitution

banTheBox.name: Colorado Chance to Compete Act
banTheBox.details: Employers with 11+ employees cannot ask about criminal history on initial application

Colorado.process: File petition in court where convicted. Filing fee required (fee waivers available). Court hearing may be required.
Colorado.notes: Colorado uses 'sealing' rather than 'expungement'. Sealed records are hidden from most background checks but not destroyed.

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: Petition to reduce to misdemeanor first under PC 17(b), then expunge
After completing sentence, petition to reduce to misdemeanor

exclusions: Felonies with state prison time (may qualify for Certificate of Rehabilitation instead)
California.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed probation and not be currently charged with or serving a sentence for any offense

banTheBox.name: California Fair Chance Act (AB 1008)
banTheBox.details: Employers with 5+ employees cannot ask about criminal history before a conditional offer of employment

California.process: File petition under PC 1203.4. No filing fee for most courts. Judge reviews and may grant without hearing.
California.notes: California calls this 'dismissal' — the guilty plea is withdrawn, a not guilty plea entered, and the case dismissed. Not a true erasure.

exclusions: Convictions (cannot be expunged, only nondisclosure for some)
Texas.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed all terms of community supervision including fines, fees, and restitution

banTheBox.name: None statewide
banTheBox.details: No statewide Ban the Box law. Some cities (Austin, San Antonio) have local ordinances for city employment.

Texas.process: File petition in court. Filing fee varies by county ($300-500). Hearing typically required.
Texas.notes: Texas distinguishes between 'expunction' (complete erasure for non-convictions) and 'nondisclosure' (sealing for deferred adjudication). Most convictions cannot be expunged.

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: 10 years after sentence completion or release

New York.sentenceCompletion: 10 years must have passed since last conviction or release from incarceration, whichever is later

banTheBox.name: New York Fair Chance Act
banTheBox.statute: NYC Admin. Code § 8-107(11-a) and NY Correction Law Art. 23-A
banTheBox.details: Employers cannot inquire about criminal history until after a conditional offer. State law prohibits unfair discrimination based on criminal history.

New York.process: File motion under CPL 160.59. No fee. DA has 45 days to respond. Court hearing may be scheduled.
New York.notes: NY allows sealing of up to 2 convictions. Sealed records still visible to law enforcement and certain licensing bodies.

eligibleOffenses.category: Cases resulting in withhold of adjudication
eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: Eligible for sealing immediately after completion
10 years after sealing, can petition for expungement

exclusions: Any prior sealing or expungement (one-time only)
Florida.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed all sentences, probation, and conditions. Must not have any pending criminal cases.

banTheBox.name: None statewide
banTheBox.details: No statewide Ban the Box law. Some counties have local ordinances.

Florida.process: Must obtain Certificate of Eligibility from FDLE ($75). Then file petition in court. One-time use only.
Florida.notes: Florida is very restrictive — you can only seal OR expunge ONE case in your lifetime. Adjudicated guilty convictions generally cannot be sealed or expunged.

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: 3 years after completion of last sentence
3 years after completion of last sentence

Illinois.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed all terms of sentence including supervision, fees, fines, and restitution

banTheBox.name: Illinois Job Opportunities for Qualified Applicants Act
banTheBox.details: Employers with 15+ employees cannot inquire about criminal history until interview or conditional offer stage

Illinois.process: File petition in circuit court. Filing fee varies. Legal aid organizations can assist for free.
Illinois.notes: Illinois distinguishes between expungement (erasure) and sealing (hidden but accessible to law enforcement). Many felonies are eligible for sealing even if not for expungement.

eligibleOffenses.category: Ungraded misdemeanors with max 2 years via Clean Slate

exclusions: All felonies (not eligible for Clean Slate auto-sealing)
Pennsylvania.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed full sentence and been free of conviction for 10 years for Clean Slate auto-sealing

banTheBox.name: Pennsylvania Criminal History Record Information Act
banTheBox.details: Employers can only consider convictions that relate to the job. Philadelphia has a stronger local Fair Chance Hiring Law.

Pennsylvania.process: Clean Slate sealing is automatic after 10 years. Traditional expungement requires filing a petition.
Pennsylvania.notes: Pennsylvania's Clean Slate Act (2018) was groundbreaking — first state with automatic sealing. Sealed records still visible to law enforcement and prosecutors.

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: 1 year after final discharge — case by case

exclusions: Domestic violence (first offense may be eligible)
Ohio.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed full sentence and all conditions including restitution, fines, and supervision

banTheBox.name: None statewide
banTheBox.details: No statewide Ban the Box law. Columbus and Cincinnati have local ordinances for city employment.

Ohio.process: File application in court of conviction. $50 filing fee. Prosecutor and victim notified. Hearing held.
Ohio.notes: Ohio expanded eligibility significantly in 2023 to allow sealing of up to 5 convictions. Previously limited to 1 felony or 2 misdemeanors.

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: 3 years after sentence completion — auto-expunge after 7 years

eligibleOffenses.category: One-bad-night provision (multiple offenses from single incident)
eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: Treated as single offense for counting purposes

exclusions: Offenses punishable by 10+ years that involved violence
Michigan.sentenceCompletion: Must have completed full sentence. Waiting period begins at completion of sentence or release from incarceration, whichever is later.

banTheBox.name: None statewide
banTheBox.details: No statewide Ban the Box law. Detroit and several counties have local ordinances.

Michigan.process: File application in court. $50 filing fee. Michigan Clean Slate Act added automatic expungement starting 2023.
Michigan.notes: Michigan's 2020 Clean Slate Act is one of the most comprehensive in the nation. Automatic expungement for eligible misdemeanors after 7 years and felonies after 10 years.

eligibleOffenses.category: Arrests without conviction (dismissals, nolle prosequi, not guilty)

eligibleOffenses.waitingPeriod: After successful completion of sentence, automatically restricted

Georgia.sentenceCompletion: Must have fully completed all terms of sentence, probation, and conditions

banTheBox.name: None statewide
banTheBox.details: No statewide Ban the Box law. Atlanta and several counties have executive orders for public employment.

Georgia.process: Apply to the arresting agency or prosecuting attorney's office. Process varies by jurisdiction.
Georgia.notes: Georgia's expungement options are quite limited for convictions. Most convictions cannot be sealed. Focus is primarily on non-conviction records and first offender treatment.
